question: Around 1713, Sawai Raja Jai Singh of Amer was appointed governor of which region?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Malwa**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• **Sawai Raja Jai Singh** of Amer, a renowned ruler from the Kachwaha dynasty, was appointed the governor of **Malwa** around **1713** by the Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar. 
 
• The region of **Malwa** was strategically important due to its location in central India, serving as a key route for trade and administrative control. 
 
• During his governorship, Jai Singh focused on administrative reforms, revenue collection, and maintaining law and order in the province. 
 
• He was also known for his contributions to architecture and astronomy, including the establishment of observatories (Jantar Mantars) in several cities. 
 
• Jai Singh's governance in Malwa was a reflection of his administrative acumen and his ability to manage diverse regions under Mughal rule. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Malwa Region:** 
 
 
• Malwa is a historical region in central India, covering parts of present-day Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. 
 
• It has been an important cultural, trade, and administrative center since ancient times, serving as a hub for rulers like the Guptas, Paramaras, and later the Mughals. 
 
 
 
• **Sawai Raja Jai Singh:** 
 
 
• Born in **1688**, Jai Singh II was a ruler of the Amer kingdom (later known as Jaipur). 
 
• He is most famous for his contributions to **astronomy** and the construction of observatories (Jantar Mantars) in cities like Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, and Varanasi. 
 
• He was a trusted ally of the Mughal emperors, and his administrative skills earned him the governorship of regions like Malwa. 
 
 
 
• **Other Regions Mentioned:** 
 
 
• **Bengal:** A crucial province in eastern India, known for its wealth and trade, but not governed by Jai Singh. 
 
• **Lahore:** A prominent city in Punjab, important during the Mughal era, but Jai Singh did not govern this region. 
 
• **Agra:** A major Mughal administrative center and the site of the famous Taj Mahal, but it was not under Jai Singh's governorship. 
 
 
 
• **Jantar Mantar Observatories:** 
 
 
• Jai Singh II constructed these observatories to advance **astronomical studies** and improve calendar-making. 
 
• The observatories are examples of **Mughal-era scientific advancements** and architectural brilliance. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• **Administrative Role:** Jai Singh II’s appointment as governor of Malwa showcases the Mughal strategy of delegating key provinces to trusted regional rulers to ensure efficient administration and loyalty. 
 
• **Astronomy and Architecture:** Jai Singh’s legacy includes his advancements in science and architecture, marking him as an innovative thinker of his time. 
 
• **Historical Impact:** His governance and contributions to Malwa had long-lasting effects on the region’s development and its integration into the Mughal empire.
